solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inexperienced horse will unseat one flapper

indicators.note: to unseat a rider is to throw them off, so a letter gets thrown out of the word

blocks.note: green means new to something, untried
horse is slang for the drug heroin
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A green young horse throws its rider and sends someone flapping through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks like the animal, but it is drug slang for heroin; dropping its I leaves HERON, so GREEN HERON.
explanation.definitionFit: A green heron is a wading bird, and any bird beating its wings in flight can be called a flapper.

clue.text: Monkey being sick must be visited by doctor

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the doctor's letters sit within the others

blocks.note: a man is a human being
sick means unwell
the standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A poorly monkey needs a house call from the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like part of the phrase 'being sick', but on its own it means a person, and the doctor's letters slip between that and sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African primate with a brightly coloured face and rump.

clue.text: Try on tops from Tiffany’s and single-breasted suit

indicators.note: the top of a word written downwards is its opening letter, so each word gives its first

blocks.note: a judge hears, or tries, a case
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Trying on clothes, perhaps jewellery from Tiffany's and a single-breasted suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like tailoring, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a standard pack of playing cards.

clue.text: European gesture primarily stirs passions

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a gesture is a motion of the hand
the first letter of stirs

explanation.surface: A continental hand gesture rouses strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Passions are strong feelings, and emotions is a general word for such feelings.

clue.text: Having gone away from island, had fun in Split

indicators.note: something that has gone away from a place is no longer there, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
to party is to have fun

explanation.surface: Back from an island holiday, someone had a great time in Split, the Croatian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Split looks like the Croatian port city, but it is the verb meaning divided.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to divide or separate, so parted means divided into pieces, the same as split.

clue.text: Thugs’ leader punches teacher in prison

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter counts
a punch drives into its target, so one piece lands inside the other

blocks.note: the first letter of thugs
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A gang boss assaults a teacher while doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is old British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is informal slang for a jail, as in the phrase doing time in stir.

clue.text: Part of song leaving one filled with ecstasy

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped out
the gap left behind is filled, so a new letter takes the vacant place

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
the Roman numeral for one
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A section of a song where the singer is overwhelmed with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of song' looks like the definition, but only 'Part' is; ARIA swaps its I for E.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or section of something, so it can stand for a part.

clue.text: Unruly masses plot to get those involved in purge

indicators.note: an unruly crowd will not keep in order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A rebellious mob conspires to overthrow the people behind a political purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purge' suggests a political clear-out, but here it means a laxative dose.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts, magnesium sulphate, are taken as a laxative, so they are the agents of a bowel purge.

clue.text: Record lout was playing could be Yellow

indicators.note: playing about with something rearranges it, so the letters get shuffled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A yob was playing a record, which could be one by the band Yellow or a song called Yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital Y makes Yellow look like the Coldplay song; it is simply the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw-coloured describes the pale golden tone of dried stalks, a shade of yellow.

clue.text: Trump is one mostly sluggish republican

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: leaden means heavy and slow
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Republican president is a lethargic Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump has been a head of state and party figurehead, an example of a person in charge.

clue.text: Go off on a conservative or revolutionary?

blocks.note: food that goes off rots
taken as written
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Should you rant about a conservative, or a radical?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a political radical, the opposite of a Tory, but here it means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory describes something that rotates, so it is revolutionary in the literal spinning sense.

clue.text: Toothy type in bondage gear cops left by lake

indicators.note: to be left by someone is to be abandoned, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: chains are used for restraint
the law is informal for the police
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A sharp-toothed character in fetish gear gets picked up by police near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The law' is informal for the police; 'left by lake' means that word loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw cuts with a loop of teeth on a chain, so it is jokingly a toothy type of thing.

clue.text: Pa is tired by his wife and children ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is wanted

blocks.note: tired means worn out or stale, as a tired joke is old
Pa's wife is Ma
the last letter of children

explanation.surface: Dad is worn out by his wife and kids in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' refers back to Pa, so his wife is MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal slang for one's father, the same as Pa.

clue.text: Isn’t Laura going out with a chap from Perth?

indicators.note: going out on the town suggests letters being jumbled up and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gossip asking whether Laura is dating a man from Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth could be the Scottish city, but the Perth here is in Western Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Perth is the capital of Western Australia, so a man from there is Australian.

clue.text: Is April honest about affairs of the heart?

indicators.note: about can mean around in disorder, so the letters are turned around

blocks.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A question of whether April is being truthful about her love life.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs of the heart are romantic involvements, and relationships is the everyday word for these.

clue.text: Retired nun tried to become something different

indicators.note: becoming something different means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A nun who has left the convent attempts a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like describing the nun, but it is the definition, meaning went to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned in is an idiom for going to bed for the night, which is another sense of retired.

clue.text: Where the Light Brigade were holding the reins?

blocks.note: first meaning: taking part in the famous cavalry charge at Balaclava
second meaning: being the person in control

explanation.walkthrough: The Charge of the Light Brigade was the doomed 1854 British cavalry attack in the Crimean War; reins suit both horses and command.
explanation.definitionFit: In charge is an idiom for being in control, and the Light Brigade were literally taking part in a cavalry charge.

clue.text: Rifleman at front going after high-flyer?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening, so only the initial letter is kept
going after means following behind, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: the snipe is a wading bird famous for its zigzag flight
the first letter of rifleman

explanation.surface: A soldier with a rifle on the front line takes aim at something flying high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifleman' serves twice: it is the definition and also supplies its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who shoots from hiding, a kind of rifleman; the word comes from shooting snipe.

clue.text: Russian autocrat hiding son in lodges

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Vladimir Putin, Russia's president
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: The Russian strongman conceals his son in a hunting lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodges' looks like a noun for cabins, but it is the verb, as in lodging a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge a claim or complaint is to formally submit it, which is what someone who puts in a claim does.

clue.text: Cops on holiday chill with heartless robbers

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is gone, so only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: someone off work is on holiday
ice is what chills a drink
the first and last letters of robbers

explanation.surface: Police on vacation relax alongside ruthless criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chill' looks like the verb to relax, but it is the noun, cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers is the formal term for cops, so officers stands in for that slang word.

clue.text: Fury shown by group of footballers and right-winger?

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body
fury is intense anger

explanation.surface: Anger from a football team and its right winger.
explanation.walkthrough: A right winger is a football position, but here it is a political label; Nigel Farage is a British right-wing politician who led UKIP and Reform UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Farage is a prominent British politician on the political right, so he is an example of a right-winger.

clue.text: Kick back, Spooner is telling you, and drink

indicators.note: William Spooner was famed for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds trade places

blocks.note: a kick is a boot and the back is the rear; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: An invitation to relax and have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick back' reads as the phrase meaning relax, but it is two separate words, kick and back.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with sassafras or other roots, popular in North America.

clue.text: Men holding a skater’s first blades

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so these letters wrap around the others
first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
taken as written
the first letter of skater

explanation.surface: Men with an ice skater's first pair of blades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blades' suggests skates, but it means the flat ends of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: The flattened end of an oar is called its blade, and rowers refer to oars as blades.

clue.text: Very entertained (initially) during assembly

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used
during means within the span of something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first letter of entertained
a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: A school assembly that was very entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Really used as an intensifying adverb, as in really good, means the same as very.

clue.text: I tucked into a porridge cooked for a beast

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into porridge made for an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' reads as eating, but it puts I and A inside the porridge letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie dog is a burrowing North American rodent, an animal and so a beast.

clue.text: One posted over in Georgia close to Roswell

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
the last letter of Roswell

explanation.surface: Someone sent to Georgia, near Roswell, the New Mexico town famous for UFO sightings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' suggests sent somewhere, but a goal is literally fitted with posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal in football or hockey is framed by two uprights, so it is jokingly a thing with posts.
